title: The two-term resolution of the finite coefficient sheaves
statement:
Let $E/\Ql$ be finite with uniformizer $\pi_E$ and $n\geq1$. For every scheme $X$
the sequence of $\mathcal O_{E,X}$-module sheaves on $X_{\Proet}$

$$
0\to\mathcal O_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\ \pi_E^n\ }\mathcal O_{E,X}\to(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X\to0
$$

is exact. Consequently, for $K\in D(X_{\Proet},\mathcal O_E)$,
$K_n=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ is
isomorphic to the cone of $\pi_E^n\colon K\to K$, naturally in $K$, and for
$1\leq m\leq n$ there are triangles
$K_m\xrightarrow{\pi_E^{n}}K_{n+m}\to K_n\to$, in particular
$K_1\to K_{n+1}\to K_n\to$.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E$, $a=\pi_E$, $B_r=A/a^rA$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] and [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect], $a\ne0$ and $B_r$ is finite. Since $|x|<|a|^r$ implies $x/a^r\in A$, the ideal $a^rA$ is open, so $B_r$ is discrete. Division is restriction of the continuous map $x\mapsto a^{-r}x$ in $E$. Apply [lem-pe-profinite-sections-finite-quotient] to get the condensed short exact sequence.

Use small site models in a larger coefficient universe. By [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], the profinite functor preserves finite limits and coverings. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] and [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-exact] make $p_X^*$ additive exact. Its module transport commutes with forgetful functors by [def-sfb-modobj-transport], hence is exact by [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-lifted]. Here tensor preserves colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed]. By [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], the resulting sequence is the asserted one over $R=A_X$, with its multiplication and reduction maps.

The free abelian cover $\bigoplus_{x\in M}\mathbf Z\to M$, $e_x\mapsto x$, is functorial and epic; its terms are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-coproduct], since tensoring with $\mathbf Z$ is the identity. By [lem-sfb-sheaf-functorial-flat-resolution], abelian sheaves have functorial flat covers. Their closed Grothendieck structure is step 2's sheaf-tensor theorem. By [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck], [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom] and [lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions], the same hypotheses hold for $R$-modules.

source.place: On X: hypotheses for unbounded derived tensor

proof.text: In this module category use [def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules]. Constant scalars give an $A$-linear structure; balancing gives $b(f\otimes g)=(bf)\otimes g=f\otimes(bg)$. Apply [lem-pe-scalar-cone-tensor-model] to $b=a^r$. The augmentation $P_b=[R\xrightarrow{b}R]\to B_{r,X}[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism by step 2. Substitution gives $K_r\cong\operatorname{Cone}(a^r:K\to K)$ naturally in $K$.

source.place: On X: two-term resolution and natural cone

proof.text: For $m,n\ge1$, define $i:B_m\to B_{n+m}$ by $[x]\mapsto[a^nx]$ and $q:B_{n+m}\to B_n$ by reduction. Changing $x$ by $a^mz$ changes $i(x)$ by $a^{n+m}z$; cancellation of $a^n\ne0$ proves injectivity. Representatives give $\ker q=\operatorname{im}i$ and surjectivity. All rings are finite discrete. Apply [lem-pe-profinite-sections-finite-quotient], then step 2, to obtain the short exact $R$-module sequence on $X$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle], step 5 gives a distinguished triangle. The K-flat left derivability structure exists by [lem-sfb-kflat-derivability] with step 3's hypotheses. Thus [lem-sc-source-kflat-tensor-left-triangulated] permits tensoring by arbitrary $K$. The vertices become $K_m,K_{n+m},K_n$; the first arrow is induced by $i$, namely the stated $\pi_E^n$. Restrict to $1\le m\le n$, then set $m=1$.
